items.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM
items.raw_content: Tool call accuracy is an important part of serving open-weight AI models. When your tool calls aren’t accurate, the model builds up on nonsensical context. We’ve been carrying our own fork of vLLM to hit 100% in tool call schema accuracy with Kimi and DeepSeek. Fortunately, vLLM 0.31 added support for constrained decoding, a technique to guarantee schema-adherence. By enabling it, you can get to 100% schema accuracy with the newer Kimi and DeepSeek models.

items.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
items.raw_content: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes tempora
items.title_zh: 视频模型的世界建模综述
items.summary: A survey uses world modeling as a unifying lens for video foundation models and video world models, organizing the literature around four operations: reading, writing, sharing and interacting.

items.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
items.raw_content: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) improves reasoning in language models, but scalar outcomes provide coarse supervision over response trajectories. Self-distillation offers denser token-level guidance by comparing an unassisted policy with a feedback-informed self-teacher, yet the teacher evolves with the student, creating unstable targets and motivating additional regularization. We introduce Function-Space Policy Optimization (FSPO), a single-policy framework that combines current privileged adaptation with function-space temporal consolidation. FSPO stores sparse historical next-token distributions as fixed temporal targets, providing temporal separation without maintaining a persistent teacher model. It further introduces privileged disagreement correction to explicitly suppress locally overvalued actions, reliability-adaptive grounding that strengthens reference
items.title_zh: 函数空间策略优化 FSPO
items.summary: FSPO is a single-policy RL framework for reasoning models that keeps sparse past next-token distributions as fixed targets over time, avoiding a persistent teacher while adding privileged disagreement correction.

items.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
items.raw_content: Agentic recommendation pursues shopper goals through sequences of context-dependent decisions. Developing and evaluating such policies requires faithful recommendation world models that capture both the interactive shopping environment and users' behavioral responses over long interactions. Existing resources rarely provide long-horizon, fine-grained real-user trajectories or support trajectory-level evaluation and offline validation against production A/B results. We introduce UserArena, a real-world e-commerce interactive benchmark containing 64,729 session trajectories from 11,010 users, spanning 566,102 items and 13 action types. UserArena pairs these trajectories with an interactive environment and supports offline validation against outcomes from a controlled production A/B test, enabling five-level evaluation from output validity and local decisions to sequential behavior, persona
items.title_zh: UserArena 购物智能体基准
items.summary: UserArena is an interactive e-commerce benchmark built from 64,729 session trajectories across 11,010 users and 566,102 items, supporting five-level evaluation and offline validation against a production A/B test.

items.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
items.raw_content: Building virtual embodied agents that operate in open-ended games like human players is a long-standing goal requiring both long-horizon autonomy and reliable native-interface control. As a procedurally generated open world, Minecraft provides a natural testbed for studying the integration of these capabilities. Existing agents typically provide either native visuomotor control without long-horizon autonomy or high-level planning executed through environment APIs or predefined skills. To bridge this gap, we propose HiSTEVE, a hierarchical VLA agent with a capability-aware agent harness. At the orchestration level, we equip the harness with structured memory for tracking progress and a VLM planner for selecting subtasks within the VLA's capabilities. To reliably determine subtask completion, we further introduce a policy-coupled task completion state detector that conditions on VLA policy
items.title_zh: HiSTEVE：开放世界游戏 VLA 智能体
items.summary: HiSTEVE is a hierarchical vision-language-action agent for open-world games like Minecraft that pairs native interface control with a capability-aware harness, structured memory and a VLM planner.

items.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
items.raw_content: We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning. With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks. Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify
items.title_zh: RynnUnify：统一具身大脑
items.summary: RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that combines spatial reasoning, physical prediction and long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video-language reasoning, with an extension for robot control.

items.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
items.raw_content: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. items.title_zh: Dual Exam：智能体与世界模型评测
items.summary: Dual Exam separately evaluates multimodal agents under fixed environment responses and world models under fixed action interventions; GPT 6 Astra leads the agent index at 31.3 and GPT-Image-2 leads full-coverage world-model scoring at 21.7.

items.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model
items.raw_content: A live esports broadcast needs a director who chooses which camera goes on air and a caster who talks over that choice, every second and without knowing what comes next. Streaming video language models have learned to commentate, but only over a broadcast that a human director has already produced. We study live broadcast production, in which a model receives the raw camera of every player and must both direct and commentate from the past alone. We present DirCast, a single streaming video language model that does both. Every second it scans all cameras at low resolution, decides with a hold-or-switch director whether and where to cut, and reads the chosen camera at high resolution before it speaks. Its context keeps what went on air and what was said and lets the other views expire, which bounds the cost of a stream of any length. We build a dataset of 27 professional Dota 2 matches wit
items.title_zh: DirCast：电竞赛事直播导演与解说
items.summary: DirCast is a single streaming video-language model that directs and commentates live esports from raw player cameras, deciding when to cut and reading the chosen view at high resolution; it was built on 27 professional Dota 2 matches.

items.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
items.raw_content: Behavior cloning for robotic manipulation is highly sensitive to the coverage of its training data, yet collecting diverse successful demonstrations remains costly. We study reinforcement learning (RL) not as a deployable controller, but as a data generator for downstream visuomotor imitation learning. Our key premise is that multiple successful solution modes cover a broader range of successful trajectories than repeatedly collecting a single narrow solution. We introduce DiscoDemo, which trains a privileged latent-conditioned RL generator with a parallel reverse curriculum and a success-gated diversity objective to discover diverse solutions while preserving task success. The trained generator produces multiple successful closed-loop behaviors, which are safety-filtered and exported as a static dataset for downstream imitation learning. Across four manipulation tasks, DiscoDemo produce
items.title_zh: DiscoDemo：发现多样机器人示范
items.summary: DiscoDemo trains a privileged latent-conditioned reinforcement learning generator with a reverse curriculum and success-gated diversity objective to produce varied successful demonstrations for robot imitation learning.

items.title: Speculative Diffusion is a Tale of Two Tradeoffs
items.raw_content: Speculative decoding is a technique that accelerates the inference speed of autoregressive large language models (LLMs) by sampling from a faster, lower quality draft model. Traditionally, a fundamental characteristic of speculative decoding is that it is lossless with respect to the verifier distribution, guaranteeing speed without sacrificing quality. This differs from recently developed diffusion LLMs (dLLMs), which are notably able to achieve substantial speedups by degrading the quality of their outputs with less diffusion effort. Because diffusion models are able to sample faster than autoregressive models by generating tokens in parallel, they are considered strong candidates for draft models in speculative diffusion. While it is widely understood that diffusion models can sacrifice quality for speed, speculative decoding itself can also be generalized to generate lossy samples fa
items.title_zh: 投机扩散的两个权衡
items.summary: The paper analyzes speculative diffusion, where diffusion models draft for autoregressive LLMs, examining the tradeoff between speed and lossless versus lossy sampling relative to the verifier.

items.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
items.raw_content: We introduce TWIG (Tree-structured Weights with Inherited Gates), a representation in which every weight of a neural network is the end of a path of small discrete decisions: a sign, a shift by a power of two, a zero gate, an index into a shared table. Weights that belong together share the upper part of their paths, and each decision is inherited by every weight below it, so it is stored once and applied once. This simple change has three consequences. Any trained network can be written as a TWIG, and when the decisions are powers of two its weight layers become circuits made almost entirely of wires and adders, suited to chips whose weights are fixed at fabrication. Pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks and weight sharing become edits of one object, so a single optimizer can choose among all of them for a whole network. And choosing the decisions is the ground-state
items.title_zh: 每个权重都是共享离散决策的路径
items.summary: TWIG represents every neural-network weight as the end of a path of shared discrete decisions - sign, power-of-two shift, zero gate and table index - so pruning, quantization and weight sharing become edits of one structure.

items.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
items.raw_content: Codes of professional ethics guide and restrict specialists, who increasingly work with assistants built on large language models. Such an assistant can breach the user's code, or help the user breach it, without the user noticing. Evaluations reporting broad categories of harm cannot show how often this happens or which provision is breached. TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests conflicting with clauses of fifteen Russian-language professional codes with benign twins that differ only in the legitimacy of what is asked. An automated pipeline generates the tasks from the text of a code, so the corpus grows with every code added and a provision yields new tasks on every run. It also produced tasks and human-validated verdicts from two English codes of other jurisdictions. In human validation of the frozen pipeline, specialists rated 0.995 of the conflicting tasks plausible, and the model judge
items.title_zh: TenetBench：职业伦理条款评测
items.summary: TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests that conflict with clauses of 15 Russian professional ethics codes with benign twins, so models can be judged on which provision they breach rather than broad harm categories.

items.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
items.raw_content: The rapid growth of microdramas has increased demand for high-quality script production. Long-form microdrama script generation with LLMs requires both diverse plot progression and long-range narrative coherence. Our observations reveal that candidate continuations increasingly concentrate on fewer narrative mechanisms as generation progresses, while conventional retrieval may reinforce trope reuse and overlook historical information essential to future plots. To address these challenges, we propose DraMaze, a multi-agent pipeline that explores diverse causal paths through trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation. It further constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to organize, retain, and retrieve historical memories based on future narrative goals. We also introduce MiDramaBench, a bilingual benchmark for evaluating script logic and creative quality across diffe
items.title_zh: DraMaze：微短剧剧本生成管线
items.summary: DraMaze is a multi-agent pipeline for long-form microdrama scripts that uses trope memory-guided tree search and a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to keep plots diverse and coherent, plus a bilingual benchmark called MiDramaBench.
